annotation.kind: direct one-based scalar-recurrence form of Lemma 3.1 and Appendix A

assumptions: The scalar sequences encode the three exact plane rotations used in Sections 2.6, 3.1.1, and Appendix A.
All indices are one-based, as in the paper, and p42PrefixProduct is the paper's product notation s^(k) or s-bar^(k).
The nonzero rho, rho-bar, and rho-tilde assumptions are exactly what is required for the displayed rotation quotients.
The structure records equations (A.1), (A.2), (A.4), (A.5), and (A.6); it does not assume the equality asserted by Lemma 3.1.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P42 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P42 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p42_t3_lsmr_transformed_components (run : P42Lemma31Run) (k : Nat) (hk : 1 <= k) : run.betaTilde k = run.tauTilde k
formal_statement.plain_language: For every positive iteration index, the transformed right-hand-side component beta-tilde equals the forward-substitution component tau-tilde, as asserted by Lemma 3.1.

informal_proof: Follow Appendix A. Prove the base case from the three rotations. Prove the product identity (A.7) for arbitrary index, derive the mixed-rotation cancellation from the squared rotation relations, and use both identities with recurrences (A.2), (A.5), and (A.6) in the induction step.
informal_statement: Prove the full arbitrary-iteration scalar recurrence identity in Lemma 3.1.

tier_rationale: The proof reconstructs a multi-stage arbitrary-index induction through three coupled rotations, including a separate product induction for (A.7), squared-rotation cancellation, sign and prefix-product bookkeeping, and the final transformed-component recurrence. It is substantial and not available from Mathlib imports. NumStability has no LSMR or matching recurrence theorem, and the exact L mathematical proof is identical to N.
